newsitem.title: USA: Allegheny Power, DQE file for merger approvals.
newsitem.headline: Allegheny Power, DQE file for merger approvals.

text.p: Allegheny Power System Inc and DQE Inc said Friday they had filed applications seeking approval of their proposed merger from federal and state regulators.

The companies said they asked the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to approve their marriage as quickly as possible, saying they had included commitments to freeze or reduce rates to help satisfy the FERC's guidelines.
They said they would offer a single transmission rate which was less than the stand-alone rates for each of the companies, and committed to set up an independent system operator.

In filings to the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission, the companies offered restructuring plans for Allegheny Power/West Penn and DQE's Duquesne Light, saying they would unbundle rates for generation, transmission and distribution services.

Duquesne Light customers will be offered a 25 percent discount on any increase in their power use, even if they choose to use another electricity supplier, and residential customers will get an average 50 percent discount for any extra power use.
The utility also offered incentives for new commercial and industrial customers, proposing to give them 20 to 25 percent discounts on their electric bills over five years.

Allegheny/West Penn said it would split any of the benefits of the merger between its shareholders and customers and agreed to freeze distribution rates until the end of Pennsylvania's transition to an open power market.

In a filing to the Maryland Public Service Commission, Allegheny Power sought approval for its stock exchange with DQE, and discussed the benefits of the merger, including lower rates over the long term and greater efficiency.
The companies plan to file later this year for approvals from the Securities and Exchange Commission, Justice Department and Federal Trade Commission.
